title: When processing an HTTP redirect to a URL containing userinfo (a username:password component), curl might erroneously retain and re-transmit the… (CVE-2026-94265)
description: A vulnerability in curl causes it to erroneously retain and resend the original host's HTTP Negotiate authentication state when processing an HTTP redirect to a URL containing userinfo (username:password). This behavior allows a malicious server to force curl to send a freshly minted Kerberos ticket to an untrusted third-party host, bypassing domain-scoping restrictions normally enforced by the absence of the --location-trusted option.
aiSummary: CVE-2026-94265 describes a flaw in curl's handling of HTTP redirects that include userinfo components. When such a redirect occurs, curl mistakenly preserves and retransmits the HTTP Negotiate authentication state from the original host. This enables an attacker controlling the redirect target to coerce curl into sending a new Kerberos ticket, generated with the client's ambient identity, to an untrusted server. This bypasses the intended domain-scoping protections that restrict Kerberos ticket transmission unless the --location-trusted flag is explicitly used.
aiImpact: An attacker can exploit this vulnerability to obtain a freshly minted Kerberos ticket from the client and send it to an untrusted third-party host. This undermines the domain-scoping restrictions designed to prevent credential leakage during HTTP redirects, potentially leading to unauthorized access or impersonation within Kerberos-authenticated environments.
